text.p: Western Australia's Brad Hogg ensured the hard work of his side's pace bowlers did not go to waste as 18 wickets fell on the opening day of their vital Sheffield Shield encounter with New South Wales on Thursday.
Hogg was the only player on either side to pass fifty as New South Wales were bundled out for 126 and Western Australia replied with 180 for eight.
The visiting team had slumped to 72 for five, New South Wales all-rounder Brad McNamara capturing three wickets in his first three overs, before Hogg provided some late resistance with 59.

New South Wales had earlier been undone by the pace of Jo Angel amd Matthew Garnaut who each took four wickets, giving their side a perfect start in a match both sides needed to win to stay in touch with leaders Queensland.
A century partnership between former test batsman David Boon and all-rounder Shaun Young rescued Tasmania from early trouble on the first day of their match against Victoria.
Boon and Young put on 100 for the fifth wicket after Tasmania had slumped to 76 for four, steering their side to 250 for six at stumps.
Boon made 75 before losing his wicket to all-rounder Ian Harvey while Young fell for 50 to Victoria captain and seam bowler Tony Dodemaide.
While Boon prospered, Ricky Ponting did little to advance his claims for a test recall against West Indies.
Ponting, dropped for the third test last month, made 26 before becoming one of Dodemaide's three victims.
